findings.claim: The supplier recorded for Lemma 3.1 is too weak. Item /48 depends on /129, but /129 only asserts that for each fixed η>0, τ(k)≤C_η k^η. Lemma 3.1 uses the maximal-order upper bound with leading constant log 2 to obtain a uniform N^0.695 bound throughout |a|≤N^(loglog(100N)). No item records that stronger supplier. E25 correctly uses it in its reason, but does not give it a status or route. The prerequisites also omit the actual cited source, Hardy–Wright Theorem 317.
findings.evidence: BKK arXiv:2007.14567v3, PDF/printed p. 18, proof of Lemma 3.1 (text and rendered page read): “τ(a) ⩽ exp((log 2 + o(1)) log a/ log log a)” and the citation [18, §18.1, Theorem 317]; reference [18] on p. 64 is Hardy–Wright, An introduction to the theory of numbers, sixth edition. The accepted /48 lists only /4 and /129 as prerequisites and asks for a maximal-order bound in its proof steps. Applying the stated /129 on the required support gives C_η N^(η loglog(100N)); no fixed η yields N^0.695 uniformly as N grows, and substituting an N-dependent η gives no control of C_η. In contrast, the source bound gives max τ(|a|)≤N^(log 2+o(1)), and 0.005+0.695−1=−0.3 recovers /48. E25 addresses 3N versus 100N, not this missing supplier item. Neither pinned tree yielded this maximal-order estimate. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5 owns divisor estimates; the reviewed AdditiveCombinatorics packet separately records an unresolved maximal-order supplier request, not an available theorem with the required constant.
findings.fix: Add a supplier theorem item asserting that for every ε>0 there is K_ε such that τ(k)≤exp((log 2+ε)log k/loglog k) for all integers k≥K_ε (with k>e). Route it once as a source to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5 through route 6 and make /48 depend on it. Alternatively strengthen /129 to include this precise bound and retain its subpower corollary for /110. Add Hardy–Wright, sixth edition, §18.1 Theorem 317 to prerequisites using the citing paper as an honest locator if the book has not been read. Update S4 and the reader to distinguish supplier extraction from deferred proof development. No supplier proof, API expansion, change to the stated Lemma 3.1, or new source erratum is requested.
